questions.q: Where does a Client Script actually execute?
options: On ServiceNow's server, inside the same engine as Business Rules
In the user's browser, the same engine that runs any web page
Inside the MID Server
It alternates between browser and server on every line
questions.explain: Client Scripts are downloaded to and executed by the browser — that's why they can reach g_form and g_user but not GlideRecord.

questions.q: A developer writes a Client Script that tries to use `GlideRecord` directly to read a record. What happens?
options: It works exactly like it would in a Business Rule
It errors, because GlideRecord is a server-side class that doesn't exist in the browser's JavaScript
It silently returns an empty result with no error
It automatically converts into a GlideAjax call
questions.explain: GlideRecord has no browser-side implementation. Direct database access from the browser isn't trusted, so GlideAjax exists specifically to bridge this gap.

questions.q: Why doesn't ServiceNow let the browser run database queries directly, per this lesson?
options: Browsers are too slow to run queries efficiently
The browser is code running on a machine ServiceNow doesn't control, and its session can be inspected or modified by the user — only the server can check ACLs on every call
GlideRecord was never ported to run in any JavaScript engine
It's a licensing restriction, not a security one
questions.explain: This is a security boundary: a user could rewrite a browser-side query via dev tools, so only the server-side engine is trusted to enforce ACLs.

questions.q: Look at this round trip: `var ga = new GlideAjax('MyScriptInclude'); ga.addParam('sysparm_name', 'myMethod'); ga.addParam('sysparm_param1', someValue);` — which step in this lesson's four-step diagram does this code represent?
options: Step 3 — the Script Include method running on the server
Step 4 — the callback reading the result
Step 1 — the Client Script preparing and naming the GlideAjax call, in the browser
This code runs entirely inside the database
questions.explain: This is step 1: the Client Script, running in the browser, builds the GlideAjax call and names which Script Include and method to invoke.

questions.q: Why is the GlideAjax round trip asynchronous rather than blocking?
options: Because the browser keeps running past the call immediately, and the result only becomes available later inside a callback, once the server actually responds
Because ServiceNow servers are too slow to respond synchronously
Asynchronous behavior is optional and can be turned off for any call
Because GlideRecord queries never return a result at all
questions.explain: The script does not pause and wait on the GlideAjax line — execution continues, and the answer only arrives later in the callback function.
